sections.h2: How large is Stamford, and why does that matter for property tax?
sections.html:
Stamford is Connecticut's largest city by area and, with 135,470 residents in the 2020 census, its second most populous after Bridgeport. It sits in Fairfield County on Long Island Sound, about 34 miles from New York City and 79 miles from Hartford.

The city covers 52.03 square miles, but only 37.62 of those are land. The other 14.41 square miles are water, which includes harbor, shoreline and several islands such as Cove Island and Grass Island. A city this big, with this much waterfront, bills a wide range of properties, from downtown to the shoreline to North Stamford above the Merritt Parkway.

That variety is why two Stamford houses of the same size can carry very different tax bills. Always look up the bill for your own parcel instead of using a citywide average.

Stamford has about 45 distinct neighborhoods and villages and two historic districts. The ones named most often include these.

  • Downtown, the South End and Harbor Point, the waterfront redevelopment
  • Shippan, Cove and Waterside along the Sound
  • Glenbrook and Springdale, which also have their own commuter rail stops
  • Turn of River, Newfield, Belltown, Ridgeway and Westover
  • North Stamford, the largest and least dense section, above the Merritt Parkway

Stamford borders Greenwich to the west, Darien to the east, New Canaan to the northeast and Pound Ridge, New York to the north. Because Greenwich and Darien are neighbors, sellers sometimes compare Stamford tax bills with theirs. The comparison is only useful if you check each town's current mill rate and assessment, which the city assessor and the neighboring towns publish.

sections.h2: What drives Stamford's economy and its tax base?
sections.html:
Corporate headquarters and financial services anchor the Stamford economy. As of 2023 the city was home to eight Fortune 500 companies, and it holds what Wikipedia calls the largest financial district in the New York region outside New York City.

Companies with headquarters or major operations in the city include Charter Communications, Philip Morris International, Synchrony Financial, Indeed, United Rentals, Gartner, Pitney Bowes and Crane Co. NBC Sports Group has its world headquarters here, and the Harbor Point project in the South End is described as one of the largest private-sector development projects in the country.

A large commercial grand list helps spread the cost of city services, but it also means residential owners should not assume their bill follows a regional pattern. Real estate in Stamford is valued parcel by parcel by the Assessor's Office.

sections.h2: What does Stamford's climate mean for a house and its value?
sections.html:
Stamford has a temperate coastal climate with hot summers and cold, variable winters. It averages about 30 inches of snow a year, compared with 45 to 60 inches in inland areas such as Hartford.

Hurricanes and tropical storms have made landfall on the Connecticut coast in 1903, 1938, 1944, 1954, 1960, 1985 (Gloria) and 2012 (Sandy). For a waterfront or low-lying property, that history is the reason flood zone status, flood insurance and storm damage repair come up in nearly every sale conversation.

If storm or fire damage has changed your house, ask the Assessor's Office whether and how that can affect the assessment, and ask before the bill arrives.

sections.h2: What are the key facts about Stamford property taxes?
sections.html:
Stamford's tax offices and due dates are listed at the top of this page. The table below adds the state rules that apply to every Connecticut sale and tells you where to confirm the local numbers.

TopicWhat to know
State law on collectionConnecticut General Statutes chapter 204 covers local levy and collection, including installments, delinquent interest and tax sales
State law on assessmentChapter 203 covers assessment and appeals
Stamford code on the conveyance form135
Conveyance returnForm OP-236, filed when the deed is recorded, for prices of $2,000 or more
Current mill rate and appeal datesNot confirmed from an opened Stamford page; ask the Assessor and Tax Collector

We did not open a current Stamford page for the mill rate or the grievance deadline, so we leave both out. Call the city offices before you make a decision that depends on them.

sections.h2: How does the state's conveyance tax work on a Stamford sale?
sections.html:
When a deed is recorded in Stamford, the seller must file a Connecticut Real Estate Conveyance Tax Return. The Department of Revenue Services says the grantor, the grantor's attorney or an authorized agent files Form OP-236, and the filing is due when the deed is recorded.

The tax applies when the consideration is $2,000 or more, and a sale using more than one deed is taxed on the total price. Participating town clerks accept electronic filing through myCTREC.

Two exemptions are worth knowing. A principal residence conveyed in lieu of foreclosure is exempt, and so is a principal residence sold for less than the mortgages plus the real estate taxes and municipal liens that rank ahead of them. A third exemption applies to certain sellers who were approved for state or local tax relief for the elderly or disabled, though the municipal portion still applies. Your closing attorney should confirm which code to enter.

sections.h2: What happens to Stamford property tax when you sell?
sections.html:
Taxes owed on the property are paid from the sale proceeds at closing, and the title or closing attorney arranges the payoff. If the current installment is not yet due or has not been billed, the attorney normally prorates it between you and the buyer.

The state's collection chapter spells out what happens if taxes are left unpaid. It includes sections on interest on delinquent installments, demand and levy, and the method of selling real estate for taxes. It also says a tax becomes uncollectible after fifteen years. Another section allows a town to add municipal expenses to a tax bill when a property violates health, safety or housing codes, so ask whether any code enforcement charge is attached to your address.

Sellers who are behind on tax often also have a mortgage in arrears, a lien from a contractor or an estate that has not been settled. Putting all payoff figures on one sheet, with the Tax Collector's written payoff and the lender's, shows you what the sale can realistically net.

sections.h2: How do Stamford's schools, transit and location affect value?
sections.html:
Stamford is on Metro-North's New Haven Line, and its station is the second busiest on the system after Grand Central Terminal. Amtrak's Acela and Northeast Regional trains also stop there. Interstate 95 and the Merritt Parkway run through the city.

Stamford Public Schools had 16,212 students in the 2022 to 2023 school year, across 13 elementary schools, five middle schools and three high schools: Westhill, Stamford High and the Academy of Information Technology and Engineering. UConn Stamford operates a campus downtown.

Glenbrook and Springdale have their own commuter rail stops on the New Canaan branch, which gives sellers there a transit point to mention.

faqs.q: Who bills property tax in Stamford, Connecticut?
faqs.a: The city's Assessor's Office values property and the Office of the Tax Collector bills and collects the tax. Confirm current due dates and the mill rate directly with those offices.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Stamford house with unpaid property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The balance, including interest, is paid from the sale proceeds at closing, and the closing attorney requests a written payoff from the Tax Collector.

faqs.q: What is the Stamford town code on the conveyance tax form?
faqs.a: The Department of Revenue Services lists 135 as the Stamford code on Form OP-236.

faqs.q: Does Connecticut tax the transfer of a house?
faqs.a: Yes. A real estate conveyance tax is due when the deed is recorded and the price is $2,000 or more, unless an exemption applies. The seller's side files the return.

faqs.q: Is a house sold for less than the debt exempt from the state conveyance tax?
faqs.a: A principal residence is exempt when the price is not enough to pay the mortgages plus the real estate taxes and municipal liens that have priority. The seller claims the exemption on the return.
The city covers 52.03 square miles, of which 37.62 are land, and had 135,470 residents in the 2020 census. It is Connecticut's largest city by area.
